subject: Biology
title: Bioenergetics of Muscle Contraction & Red vs. White Fibers
learningObjectives: Differentiate ATP generation by Phosphagen, Anaerobic Glycolytic, and Aerobic pathways
Describe the role of the Cori Cycle in resolving lactic acidosis
Compare Type I Red vs Type II White muscle fibers in biochemical and physiological traits
content:
### 5.1 Muscle ATP Regeneration Pathways

```
                           MUSCLE ATP SOURCES
                                    │
         ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┐
         ▼                          ▼                          ▼
  STORED ATP & CREATINE PHOSPHATE  ANAEROBIC GLYCOLYSIS       AEROBIC RESPIRATION
  ├── Direct ATP (2–3 seconds)     ├── Glycogen ──► Lactic Acid ├── Oxidative Phosphorylation
  └── Creatine Phosphate + ADP     └── Rapid, yields 2 ATP     └── Mitochondria (Myoglobin O₂)
      ──[Creatine Kinase]──► ATP       Causes Muscle Fatigue       Sustained contraction
```

1. **Phosphagen System (Creatine Phosphate)**: High-energy phosphate buffer sustaining maximal contraction for 2–8 seconds:
   $$\text{Creatine Phosphate} + \text{ADP} \xrightarrow{\text{Creatine Kinase}} \text{Creatine} + \text{ATP}$$
2. **Anaerobic Glycolysis (Glycogen-Lactic Acid Pathway)**: Fast ATP supply during explosive bursts; produces lactic acid that is transported to the liver via the **Cori Cycle** to regenerate glucose.
3. **Aerobic Respiration**: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation utilizing oxygen stored in **Myoglobin** for continuous, non-fatiguing muscle activity.

### 5.2 Red (Slow-Twitch) vs. White (Fast-Twitch) Muscle Fibers

| Trait | Red Muscle Fibers (Type I / Slow-Twitch) | White Muscle Fibers (Type II / Fast-Twitch) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Myoglobin Content** | **High** (imparts deep red color) | **Low** (pale or white appearance) |
| **Mitochondria Count** | **Abundant / Numerous** | Sparse / Few |
| **Vascularization** | Dense capillary beds | Sparse capillaries |
| **Sarcoplasmic Reticulum** | Moderately developed | **Extensively developed** (rapid $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ release) |
| **Primary Metabolism** | **Aerobic Respiration** (Oxidative Phosphorylation) | **Anaerobic Glycolysis** |
| **Contraction Kinetics** | Slow contraction velocity; **Fatigue-Resistant** | Rapid, powerful contraction; **Fatigues Quickly** |
| **Physiological Examples** | Postural back muscles, flight muscles of migratory birds | Extraocular eye muscles, muscles of human hands/digits |

conceptBreakdown.heading: The Cori Cycle in Muscle Bioenergetics
conceptBreakdown.explanation: During strenuous anaerobic exercise, muscle glycogen is converted into lactate. Lactate diffuses into the bloodstream and reaches the liver, where hepatic gluconeogenesis converts it back into glucose (consuming 6 ATP equivalents) to replenish muscle glycogen stores.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Oxygen Debt (EPOC)
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Following heavy exercise, elevated oxygen consumption persists (Excess Post-Exercise Oxygen Consumption) to replenish ATP, phosphocreatine, and myoglobin O2 stores, and clear accumulated lactic acid.
